strings.l1_lesson1_step2_body: Der Rahmen außen hält alles zusammen. Der Balken quer in der Mitte heißt MITTELSTEG. Er trennt oben und unten!

l1_rod_heaven_earth.one: %1$s: obere Perle unten + %2$d untere Perle oben
l1_rod_heaven_earth.other: %1$s: obere Perle unten + %2$d untere Perlen oben

notes.l1_lesson1_step2_body: „Stange“ is almost the same word as „Stab“ (the rods that hold the beads), so a child could mix up the beam with the rods; chunk 02 (tour_step_03) already calls the beam „Balken“ / „Mittelsteg“, use the same.
notes.l1_phase_practice: Glossary decision chunk 04: the Practice STEP inside a lesson (Lernen / Üben / Quiz) is „Üben“; „Training“ is reserved for the app's Abacus Practice mode (Abakus-Training).
notes.l1_practice_complete: Same rule: „Training“ is the app mode, this card closes the „Üben“ step of a lesson; „Fertig geübt!“ is the natural child wording and also fits the Level 2 practice screen that reuses the key.
notes.l1_rod_zero: Factual error carried over from the English: for 0 the upper bead stays UP, so „alle Perlen unten“ is wrong. Glossary rule for all new languages: „all beads away from the beam“, same wording as l1_instr_zero / l1_lesson2_step1_body („weg vom Mittelsteg“).
notes.l1_rod_heaven_earth: „obere Perle + 2 untere Perlen oben“ lets the final „oben“ attach to the upper bead as well (upper bead UP = not counted); „obere Perle unten“ states where the 5-bead sits, as in l1_rod_heaven („nur die obere Perle unten“).
